Dell validation remains a required post-finish shared-business-workflow and adoption gate, but Dell availability does not gate completion of system design, the council audit, or entry into non-production construction.
proposed_rulings.preserved_boundary: Dell remains an equal operator of shared business records; this ruling concerns system-design sequencing only and does not weaken later two-partner workflow acceptance.

proposed_rulings.conflict: Mature End State snapshot lines 897-900 define G0 as Approved and Ready and G1 as Trustworthy foundation; its Phase 0 action register at lines 1028-1045 mixes preconstruction planning with release-truth construction. Workspace snapshot lines 942-954 treat Phase 0 as the program/readiness gate and Phase 1 as website foundation acceptance.
proposed_rulings.recommended_ruling: Reserve Phase 0 for planning, inventories, contracts, runnable synthetic prototypes, council reconciliation, and Joe approval through G0. Rename baseline P0 construction programs as Foundation work packages. Phase 1 begins at G1 with clean release truth, isolated staging, CI, artifact provenance, environment auth, audit correlation, and restore rehearsal before product vertical slices.
proposed_rulings.entry_rule: Phase 1 may start immediately after council recommendation, Joe approval, all Phase 0 machine checks, Joe's six uncoached Workspace journeys and six uncoached Control Room flows, five baseline collection methods ready without invented values, and every material fork either decided or deferred with a named reopen trigger.

proposed_rulings.conflict: Mature End State snapshot lines 750-753 and Production Maturity Baseline snapshot lines 543-547 and 966-970 require isolated Staging, while Control Room snapshot lines 358, 406, and 1010 describe Staging as planned and recommend rehearsal branches first.
proposed_rulings.recommended_ruling: Adopt a persistent isolated Staging environment as a G1 requirement. Rehearsal remains a distinct earlier safety environment and must not be relabeled as Staging. Staging must be proven unable to access Production data or credentials and must publish intentional drift.
proposed_rulings.preserved_boundary: Until Staging exists, every product and UI must show it as Planned/Unknown and production mutation remains closed.

proposed_rulings.conflict: Workspace snapshot line 835 says subagents do not commit unless explicitly authorized, while the current standing rule requires every session to commit and push only its explicit paths. workspace/contracts/environment-release-process.v1.json also carries the obsolete no-commit/no-push wording.
proposed_rulings.recommended_ruling: The current standing rule controls: each delegated coding session uses an isolated worktree or explicitly owned paths, stages explicit paths, runs proportional verification, commits its own completed scope, and pushes its branch when available. Deployment, production writes, external communication, and merges remain separately authorized actions.
proposed_rulings.preserved_boundary: A commit is evidence packaging, not merge, deploy, production-write, or expansion of task scope.

proposed_rulings.conflict: control-room/contracts/council-review.v1.json allows only accept_recommendation, choose_alternative, or defer_with_named_external_blocker. A valid evidence-gated deferral can depend on an internal measurement or scheduled review rather than an external blocker.
proposed_rulings.recommended_ruling: Add defer_with_named_reopen_trigger. Every deferral must name the exact trigger, owner, due or observation condition, affected construction scope, and safe interim default. Deferral must never imply approval or silently unblock construction.

proposed_rulings.conflict: Joe's proposal correctly identifies the need for persistent agent presence, but it also gives Hermes durable memory, self-modifying skills, shared full MCP access, multi-channel delivery, scheduling, and Portal hosting before CARR's server-side authority, privacy, retention, isolation, and evidence gates have been proven for that runtime.
proposed_rulings.recommended_ruling: Approve the constrained Nous Portal Cloud-hosted, dedicated-container, R0 read-only Hermes evaluation defined in phase0/hermes-runtime-council-candidate.v1.json and accept its proposed mature role split: Hermes orchestrates routine CARR operations behind Doc and product controls, while Claude Code and Codex are reserved for construction, complex investigation, new features, and reviewed repairs. Treat Hermes memory and skills as non-authoritative working state, enable Privacy Mode, send only minimum-necessary data, and keep scheduling, engineering dispatch, delivery, and mutation absent from the evaluation. Joe accepts the incremental model-data exposure; persistent credential, execution, retention, recovery, export, and cost gates remain load-bearing. Expansion requires observed 30, 60, and 90-day like-for-like cost, quality, toil, and routine-displacement evidence; forecast ROI is not adoption evidence.
proposed_rulings.preserved_boundary: CARR MCP, Doctrine, Neon, and the record layer remain the kernel, source of truth, and authority plane; Doc remains the human-facing product identity; Hermes may orchestrate only through typed graduated capabilities; Claude Code and Codex remain the engineering plane; every later mutation or external effect remains server-authorized, plan-bound, human-approved, audited, and freshly verified.

proposed_rulings.conflict: CARR is Joe's current employer and launch organization, while the mature software and IP are intended to remain owner-controlled and potentially licensable to other isolated tenants. Retaining CARR as the permanent platform identity would bind Joe-owned software to one employer and deepen rename debt during construction.
proposed_rulings.recommended_ruling: Approve the independent naming architecture in phase0/platform-naming-council-candidate.v1.json: choose a distinct platform name before production construction, preserve CARR as the launch tenant and familiar branding configuration, and run a bounded evidence-backed name-selection sprint after Joe approves the council output. Do not choose or propagate a final name without trademark, domain, registry, app-store, similarity, usability, and migration checks.
proposed_rulings.preserved_boundary: Renaming does not authorize public SaaS, billing, signup, a tenant selector, source transfer, commercial rollout, or construction. Joe retains platform/IP/root/release/licensing authority, and tenant identity remains server-derived.

proposed_rulings.conflict: CARR has more than 150 human real estate agents, including solo agents and teams. Treating a CARR company-tenant seat as tenant-wide business-data authority would expose Panhandle-specific or other agents' records, search, files, calls, memory, queues, integrations, audit, exports, offline packs, and product projections.
proposed_rulings.recommended_ruling: Pre-engineer one CARR company-tenant architecture with isolated business workspaces while only Joe and Dell operate Panhandle Team. A human seat grants authentication and licensed modules but zero business-data access. A future solo agent could receive a private workspace; a future real estate team could receive a workspace with explicit individual memberships and attribution. Every request is bound to one server-derived active workspace, and cross-workspace collaboration uses typed minimum-field shares rather than ambient visibility.
proposed_rulings.preserved_boundary: This is cheap structural preparation, not a rollout or commercialization decision. Tenant administration grants no business-data access; Doc and Hermes cannot widen the human's active workspace; company reporting is purpose-built and minimum-field. No additional CARR user onboarding, public SaaS, signup, billing, client portal, or tenant-wide book search is authorized.

proposed_rulings.conflict: The mature architecture places authority in Neon and system definitions in Git, and Dell already operates without a CARR AI vault. Yet README, repo-to-vault mappings, Drive-synchronized skills, Cowork launchers, calendar exchange files, compiled projections, hooks, health checks, and other file-mode consumers still preserve Google Drive as a transitional runtime dependency. The existing reconciliation describes some Drive fallbacks as continuing without naming their final retirement target.
proposed_rulings.recommended_ruling: Approve the Drive-free target defined in phase0/drive-free-system-council-candidate.v1.json. No Drive file may be required to boot, authorize, schedule, operate, observe, recover, or reconstruct the platform. Retire Cowork as an operational dependency. Put deterministic recurring work in repo-defined code on registered Local Edge Nodes; make Hermes the preferred persistent routine-operations and Doc orchestrator after its graduated gates; reserve Claude Code and Codex for engineering. Preserve Google Drive only as an optional user-selected human document destination whose absence cannot degrade core system health.
proposed_rulings.joe_position: Hermes is the game-changing cloud orchestration layer that makes the Drive-free, Cowork-independent direction practical.
proposed_rulings.preserved_boundary: Drive independence is a property of Neon, GitHub, Cloudflare/KV/R2, typed MCP, and registered Local Edge Nodes, not a dependency on Hermes. A Hermes or Portal outage cannot force Drive fallback, change authority, or impair canonical recovery. Do not silently expand the August 21 doctrine cutoff or delete transitional consumers before inventory, parity, rollback, and disconnected-operation evidence passes.

proposed_rulings.conflict: Workspace and Tour Mode define business records, locked appointments, routing, and offline tours, but the canonical Workspace roadmap does not yet define one whole-market spatial operating surface across prospects, active clients, in-process and active projects, and visits. Without a location-role model, records with several sites, unlocated records, geocode vendor terms, and route proposals can become silent omissions or a shadow source of truth.
proposed_rulings.recommended_ruling: Approve phase0/workspace-market-map-council-candidate.v1.json as a formal Workspace roadmap amendment. Create one tenant- and workspace-scoped Market Map and Day-Trip Planner with exact accessible map/list parity; separate entity class from practice/current, target area, candidate, confirmed-site, and visit-stop location roles; report current/stale/Unknown/unlocated component counts; keep vendor-derived geocodes and routes isolated and versioned; preserve locked appointments; exclude ineligible stops with reasons while routing eligible stops; and require Joe or Dell confirmation before the existing Tour lifecycle.
proposed_rulings.preserved_boundary: The map is a read projection and planning workspace, never a canonical record writer. Whole-market access is absent in sterile/client-facing mode. Google remains only the preferred measured routing direction until terms, retention, map compatibility, attribution, portability, price, usage caps, tenant/workspace denial, accessibility, and Joe/Dell uncoached adoption pass. Phase 0 uses synthetic data and grants no production construction or vendor-purchase authority.
